findings.summary: Q7's idempotent/safe definitions and Q8's retry fix are introduced before the Idempotency-Key concept is explained, and Q8 asserts the fix with no example.
findings.evidence: "Fix POST retries with an Idempotency-Key"
findings.fix: Add a forward pointer such as "(see Q42)", or state in one line what the key does (the server replays the saved response for a repeated key).

findings.summary: Q13 says failed authentication gives 401 and failed authorization gives 403, but the 401/403 distinction on page 4 is the only place that explains the codes, and the Q15 JWT/session comparison uses 'revoke' before Q16 explains revocation.
findings.evidence: "Session: cookie holds ID, server looks it up; token: server verifies signature" / "Tokens scale across servers; sessions revoke easily"
findings.fix: Add a short line in Q15 saying that revocation means invalidating a token before it expires, or point to Q16.

findings.summary: Q18 uses the 'authorization code' and 'back channel' without explaining the flow in order, and PKCE in Q20 is introduced as 'stops a stolen code' when the code-theft risk was never shown.
findings.evidence: "Code travels in the browser; token goes over the back channel." / "==PKCE== stops a stolen code being redeemed"
findings.fix: In Q18, add the ordered steps: the user approves, the redirect carries the code, then the backend exchanges it. In Q20, state that the code can be intercepted in the redirect.

findings.summary: Q21 (CORS) relies on credentials and cookies before CSRF and SameSite are defined in Q24, and Q24 has no example despite two attacks needing one.
findings.evidence: "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true" / "Bearer tokens in headers avoid CSRF; defend cookies with SameSite"
findings.fix: Add an example to Q24 (a forged form POST to a bank, an injected script tag) and define SameSite in one line.

findings.summary: Q40 relies on 'retries' and 'dedupe by event id' before idempotency is taught on page 12, and Q38's bullets are garbled into mixed comparison fragments that confuse the order of the comparison.
findings.evidence: "Goal: spread load vs API policy; knows hosts, health vs routes, users, keys"
findings.fix: Add a forward pointer from Q40 to idempotency (Q41), and rewrite Q38 as a clean two-sided comparison.

findings.summary: The Idempotency-Key header is used in the payments example of Q41 before Q42 explains how it works, and Q42 has no example showing a request replay.
findings.evidence: "Idempotency-Key: 7f3a-91c2" (Q41) / "Same key, different body: return **422**" (Q42, no example)
findings.fix: Add an example to Q42 showing the first POST returning 201, then the retry returning the same body with the same status.

findings.summary: Q53's design answer asserts 'base62 counter avoids collisions' and 302 vs 301 without explaining the difference or showing a code-generation example, and Q55's fan-out on write/read is used with no definition.
findings.evidence: "Fan out on write for normal users, on read for celebrities"
findings.fix: Define fan-out on write (copy a post into each follower's feed at write time) vs on read (assemble the feed at request time), and note that 301 is cached by browsers while 302 is not.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a generic topic statement rather than a hook that creates curiosity or stakes.
findings.evidence: "The API interview questions they will ask you, answered in handwritten notes."
findings.fix: Open with a concrete hook, e.g. "Most backend candidates fumble the same API questions: idempotency, JWT vs OAuth, rate limiting. Here are the answers."

findings.summary: Hashtags #systemdesign and #iolar are weakly tied to the content, since the carousel covers API interview questions, not system design, and #iolar is a brand tag.
findings.evidence: "#systemdesign", "#iolar"
findings.fix: Replace #systemdesign with a relevant tag such as #apidesign or #backendinterview, and keep #iolar only if it is an intentional brand tag.

findings.summary: The cover claims more Q&As than the handbook contains.
findings.evidence: "60+ handwritten Q&As" while the questions run Q1 to Q56
findings.fix: Change to "56 handwritten Q&As" or "50+ handwritten Q&As".

findings.summary: The claim that re-login can never fix a 403 is overstated, because logging in as a different, more privileged user can resolve it.
findings.evidence: "Re-login can fix 401, never 403"
findings.fix: Say "Re-login as the same user won't fix 403; the role or scope must change".

findings.summary: Q14 uses 'HMAC/RSA' and 'claims' with no definition, and the table on this page is placed before the JWT refresh and revocation material it summarises.
findings.evidence: "{green:Signature} (HMAC/RSA) proves no tampering"
findings.fix: Gloss 'claims' as 'fields in the payload', and mention that HS256 uses a shared secret while RS256 uses a key pair.

findings.summary: Keyset pagination is described as a constant-time seek, but a B-tree index seek is O(log n).
findings.evidence: "Keyset seeks via an index in constant time"
findings.fix: Say "Keyset seeks via an index (O(log n)), so cost does not grow with page depth".

findings.summary: Q25 mentions 'cursor' and a cursor value before the keyset idea is introduced, and Q26 introduces 'Keyset' as a term with no definition.
findings.evidence: "Keyset seeks via an index in constant time"
findings.fix: Define keyset as 'cursor pagination on an indexed column (WHERE id > last_seen)' in Q25 or Q26.

findings.summary: The rate limiting diagram appears before token bucket and the window algorithms, and the Q32 reference to a gateway uses a concept not taught until page 11.
findings.evidence: "Atomic `INCR` or Lua script avoids races; or enforce at gateway"
findings.fix: Add a forward pointer ("gateway, see Q37") or move the gateway mention to the gateway page.

findings.summary: Q33 uses 'CDN' and 'Cache-Control private/public, s-maxage' in the example before Q34 explains Cache-Control, and the 304 revalidation flow in Q34 omits how the ETag first reaches the client.
findings.evidence: "Cache-Control: private, max-age=60" (Q33) / "Client sends `If-None-Match` with the saved ETag"
findings.fix: Add the first response's `ETag: "v42"` header to the Q34 example, and move the Cache-Control example after Q34.

findings.summary: The gateway/load balancer relationship is stated backwards. Load balancers usually sit in front of gateway instances.
findings.evidence: "gateways often front several LBs"
findings.fix: Say "a load balancer often fronts several gateway instances", or drop the clause.

findings.summary: The Deprecation header example uses the obsolete boolean form, and the Sunset value is not a valid HTTP-date.
findings.evidence: "Deprecation: true" and "Sunset: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 GMT"
findings.fix: RFC 9745 defines Deprecation as a Structured Field Date, e.g. "Deprecation: @1767225600". Sunset (RFC 8594) needs a full HTTP-date with a time: "Sunset: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 00:00:00 GMT".

findings.summary: Q44 says 'Idempotency keys make retries safe; versions make change safe', a point that belongs to the page theme but appears as a stray bullet inside the breaking-change answer, and the Sunset/Deprecation headers are asserted with only a bare example.
findings.evidence: "Idempotency keys make retries safe; versions make change safe"
findings.fix: Move that sentence to the key takeaways, and show a full deprecation response with a `Link` header to the migration guide.

findings.summary: Q45 uses 'object storage' and 'checksum' before Q46 explains presigned URLs, which is how the client actually sends bytes direct to storage.
findings.evidence: "Send ==chunks== straight to object storage; the API never buffers the file"
findings.fix: Swap Q45 and Q46, or add a forward pointer to Q46 explaining how the client gets permission to write to storage.

findings.summary: Q50 introduces traces and 'span' (used in Q52) without defining a span, and Q49's p50/p95/p99 percentiles are used without explanation.
findings.evidence: "Duration: p50, p95, p99, never just average"
findings.fix: Define a percentile (p99 = 99% of requests are faster than this) and a span (one timed step inside a trace).

findings.summary: The cheatsheet says 429 always includes Retry-After, but the standard only says a 429 response MAY include it.
findings.evidence: "429 always pairs with Retry-After"
findings.fix: Write "429 should include Retry-After" or "429 usually pairs with Retry-After".

findings.summary: The cheatsheet's rate-limit code example puts `Cache-Control: no-store` on a 429, an unexplained header that was never taught for rate limits, and the table lists 'PATCH maybe' where page 3 said 'Usually no'.
findings.evidence: "Cache-Control: no-store" / "["PATCH","no","maybe","200"]"
findings.fix: Remove the Cache-Control line from the 429 example, or add a note on why; make PATCH consistent with Q7 (not guaranteed idempotent).
